title: ArcGIS Pro (sample exam)
description: Sample questions on core ArcGIS Pro skills. Not official Esri exam content; each answer links to the ArcGIS Pro documentation.

bundles.title: Bundle 1: Projects, maps and layouts
bundles.description: Projects, the Contents pane, scenes, symbology, labelling, coordinate systems, layouts and sharing.

questions.question: Which file extension does an ArcGIS Pro project file use?
questions.explanation: ArcGIS Pro projects are saved as .aprx files. .mxd is an ArcMap document, .lyrx is a layer file and .ppkx is a project package.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Create a project

questions.question: By default, which items does ArcGIS Pro create alongside a new project?
answers: A file geodatabase (<project name>.gdb) and a toolbox (<project name>.atbx) in a new home folder
An enterprise geodatabase connection and a Python toolbox
A mobile geodatabase and a layer file for each map
Nothing; you must add a geodatabase and toolbox manually
questions.explanation: A new project gets a home folder containing a default file geodatabase and a default toolbox, both named after the project. Geoprocessing output and models are saved there unless you choose otherwise.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Create a project

questions.question: You need to send a colleague a single file containing your project, its maps and its data. What do you create?
questions.explanation: A project package bundles the project and the data it references into one .ppkx file that can be shared and unpacked by another ArcGIS Pro user.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Share a project package

questions.question: Which Contents pane tab do you use to change the order in which layers draw?
questions.explanation: The Drawing Order tab arranges layers in the order they display in the map. Drag a layer to reposition it.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Contents pane

questions.question: In the Contents pane's Drawing Order view, how does a layer at the top of the list display?
answers: It draws above the layers listed below it
It draws beneath all other layers
Its position in the list has no effect on drawing
questions.explanation: Layers at the top of the Drawing Order list draw above those below them.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Contents pane

questions.question: Your 3D data uses a local projected coordinate system for a city. Which scene viewing mode is recommended?
questions.explanation: Global scenes support only WGS 84 and CGCS 2000. If the data is in another spatial reference, a local scene is recommended to avoid distortion from reprojection.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Scenes

questions.question: Which geographic coordinate systems do global scenes support?
questions.explanation: Global scenes support the WGS 84 and CGCS 2000 geographic coordinate systems. Use a local scene for other spatial references.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Scenes

questions.question: Which layout element displays the contents of a map or scene on a layout?
questions.explanation: A map frame is the layout element that shows a map or scene. Legends, scale bars and other map surrounds are linked to a map frame.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Add and modify map frames

questions.question: In a spatial map series, what defines the map extent of each page?
answers: A feature in the index layer
The extent of the default basemap
A page number field in the project
questions.explanation: A spatial map series iterates through the features of an index layer, creating one page per feature. Each page's extent comes from its feature.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Introduction to spatial map series

questions.question: You want a layer to show only parcels where ZONE = 'Residential', without changing the source data. What do you use?
questions.explanation: A definition query filters which features a layer displays and uses. The underlying data is not altered.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Filter features with definition queries

questions.question: Which classification method creates class breaks from natural groupings inherent in the data?
questions.explanation: Natural breaks (Jenks) groups similar values and maximises differences between classes. The breaks are data-specific, so they are not ideal for comparing maps built from different data.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Data classification methods

questions.question: Classification methods such as quantile and equal interval apply to which kind of field?
answers: Numeric fields used for graduated symbology
Text fields used for unique values symbology
questions.explanation: Classification methods group numeric field values into classes for graduated symbology.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Data classification methods

questions.question: You want highways and local roads in the same layer labelled with different text symbols. What do you configure?
answers: Multiple label classes, each with an SQL query
Two definition queries on the same layer
A separate map for each road type
A coded value domain on the road type field
questions.explanation: Label classes let you label subsets of features in one layer with different properties. An SQL query on each class determines which features it labels.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Use label classes

questions.question: You add layers with different coordinate systems to one map. What does ArcGIS Pro do?
answers: Projects them on the fly to the map's coordinate system for display, without changing the source data
Permanently reprojects the source data to match the first layer
Refuses to add layers whose coordinate system differs from the map
Displays each layer in its own coordinate system, so they do not align
questions.explanation: The map has a single coordinate system. Layers in other coordinate systems are projected on the fly for display; use the Project tool if you need to change the data itself.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Coordinate systems, map projections, and transformations

questions.question: Where do you set a map's coordinate system directly by choosing one from a list?
answers: Map Properties dialog box, Coordinate Systems tab
Layer Properties dialog box, Source tab
questions.explanation: Right-click the map in the Contents pane, click Properties, then open the Coordinate Systems tab of the Map Properties dialog box.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Work with coordinate systems

questions.question: Which type of coordinate system locates features using latitude and longitude in angular units?
questions.explanation: A geographic coordinate system uses angular units (degrees) on a three-dimensional model of the earth. A projected coordinate system uses linear units on a flat surface.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Coordinate systems, map projections, and transformations

questions.question: What does a bookmark in a map save?
answers: A geographic location (extent) you can navigate back to
A copy of the selected features
A snapshot of the attribute table
questions.explanation: Bookmarks save map locations so you can return to them later. They can also drive a bookmark map series on a layout.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Bookmarks

questions.question: Which tool selects features based on an SQL query of their attribute values?
questions.explanation: Select Layer By Attribute adds, updates or removes a selection using an attribute (SQL) query. Select Layer By Location selects using spatial relationships.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Select Layer By Attribute (Data Management Tools)

questions.question: You want your ArcGIS Pro map to open in Map Viewer in ArcGIS Online. What do you share?
questions.explanation: Sharing a web map publishes the map's layers and saves a web map item that opens in Map Viewer and web apps. A map package is for ArcGIS Pro users.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Share a web map

questions.question: When you share a web feature layer to ArcGIS Online, what type of layer is created?
answers: A hosted feature layer, with the data copied to ArcGIS Online
A map image layer that references your local data
A tile layer cached from your map
A layer file stored in your project folder
questions.explanation: Sharing a web feature layer to ArcGIS Online copies all data and creates a hosted feature layer. You need privileges to publish hosted feature layers.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Share a web feature layer

bundles.title: Bundle 2: Geodatabases and geoprocessing
bundles.description: Geodatabase types, domains, subtypes, relationship classes, editing, analysis tools, ModelBuilder and ArcPy.

questions.question: How is a file geodatabase stored on disk?
answers: As a collection of files in a folder
As tables in SQL Server or Oracle
questions.explanation: A file geodatabase is a collection of files in a folder (with a .gdb extension) that stores, queries and manages spatial and nonspatial data.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: File geodatabases

questions.question: Which geodatabase type is stored in an SQLite database as a single file?
questions.explanation: Mobile geodatabases are stored in SQLite, a single cross-platform file on disk, which makes them portable and good for data exchange.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Mobile geodatabases

questions.question: What must all feature classes in a feature dataset share?
questions.explanation: A feature dataset is a collection of related feature classes that share a common coordinate system. Feature datasets are needed for controller datasets such as topology and parcel fabrics.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Create and manage feature datasets in ArcGIS Pro

questions.question: Which geodatabase element restricts a field to a specified list of valid values, each with a description?
questions.explanation: A coded value domain specifies a set of valid values. Each code (for example 1) has a user-friendly description (for example Pavement). A range domain sets a valid minimum and maximum instead.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Introduction to attribute domains

questions.question: When you add a subtype with the Add Subtype tool, what data type is the subtype code?
questions.explanation: Each subtype has a unique integer code and a text description.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Add Subtype (Data Management Tools)

questions.question: In a composite relationship class, what happens to related destination objects when you delete an origin object?
answers: Their foreign key is set to Null
They are moved to a new origin object
questions.explanation: In a composite relationship, destination objects cannot exist independently of the origin, so deleting the origin deletes them. In a simple relationship, the destination's foreign key is set to Null instead.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Geodatabase relationship class types

questions.question: Which pane do you use to create new features from feature templates?
questions.explanation: The Create Features pane lists feature templates for editable layers. Choose a template and a construction tool to create features.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Introduction to creating features

questions.question: Which geoprocessing environment limits processing to features or rasters that fall within a set area?
questions.explanation: The Extent environment defines the area that tools process. Only data within the extent is processed.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Extent (environment setting)

questions.question: You run Clip on roads using a council boundary. Which attributes does the output contain?
answers: Only the attributes of the input (roads) features
Only the attributes of the clip (boundary) features
questions.explanation: Clip output contains all the attributes of the input features. Use Intersect if you need attributes from both inputs.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Clip (Analysis Tools)

questions.question: Which tool computes the geometric intersection of input features and keeps attributes from all inputs?
questions.explanation: Intersect writes features or parts of features that overlap in all inputs, with attributes from each input.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Intersect (Analysis Tools)

questions.question: In the Buffer tool, what does a Dissolve Type of All do?
answers: Merges all buffers into a single feature, removing overlaps
Keeps a separate buffer for every input feature
Dissolves buffers only where attributes in a list of fields match
Deletes buffers that overlap other buffers
questions.explanation: Dissolve Type All combines all buffers into a single feature with no overlap. None keeps individual buffers; List dissolves by shared values in chosen fields. With All or List, the output does not include the BUFF_DIST or ORIG_FID fields.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Buffer (Analysis Tools)

questions.question: Which tool aggregates features based on matching values in one or more specified fields?
questions.explanation: Dissolve aggregates features that share the same values in the dissolve fields, optionally calculating summary statistics.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Dissolve (Data Management Tools)

questions.question: You need each address point to carry the name of the suburb polygon it falls in, written to a new output. Which tool do you use?
questions.explanation: Spatial Join transfers attributes from join features to target features based on a spatial relationship and writes the result to a new feature class.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Spatial Join (Analysis Tools)

questions.question: What is the key difference between a join and a relate?
answers: A join appends the other table's fields to the layer; a relate defines a link without appending fields
A join is permanent; a relate is temporary
A join works only on spatial data; a relate works only on tables
A join needs a common field; a relate does not
questions.explanation: Both use a common key field. A join appends the fields of one table to another; a relate defines a relationship you can follow without appending fields.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Introduction to joins and relates

questions.question: You need to select all parcels that intersect a flood zone polygon. Which tool do you use?
questions.explanation: Select Layer By Location selects features based on a spatial relationship (such as Intersect) to features in another layer.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Select Layer By Location (Data Management Tools)

questions.question: What is ModelBuilder?
answers: A visual programming language for building geoprocessing workflows
A tool for building 3D building models
A Python package for machine learning
A wizard for creating geodatabase schemas
questions.explanation: ModelBuilder is a visual programming language for building geoprocessing workflows that automate and document analysis and data management processes.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: What is ModelBuilder?

questions.question: Which Python site package gives access to ArcGIS Pro geoprocessing tools?
questions.explanation: ArcPy is the Python site package that provides geoprocessing tools, functions, classes and modules for ArcGIS Pro.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Introduction to ArcPy

questions.question: Where can you review and re-open geoprocessing tools you have already run in a project?
questions.explanation: Each tool you run adds an entry under the Geoprocessing tab of the History pane. Open it from Analysis > Geoprocessing > History.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Geoprocessing history

questions.question: What do raster pyramids do?
answers: Store lower-resolution copies of a raster to speed up display
Compress a raster to reduce file size
Convert a raster to 3D for scenes
Store statistics used for symbology stretches
questions.explanation: Pyramids are reduced-resolution copies of a raster. They speed up display by drawing only the resolution needed at the current scale.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Raster pyramids

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an expression type for the Calculate Field tool?
questions.explanation: Calculate Field supports Python, Arcade, SQL and VBScript expressions. C# is not supported.

source.title: ArcGIS Pro documentation: Calculate Field (Data Management Tools)
